en: So let's take a look at the agent.py file,
which is the main logic for this agent. We
also got agent_tools, which you guessed it,
includes the tools the agent can use. We'll
take a brief look at that as well, but let's
start with agent.py.
We got some imports at the top, most
importantly the OpenAI SDK, which allows us
to talk to the OpenAI API and send requests
to their models and use their models as a
brain.
Then from agent_tools, I'm importing some
tools and that's not some third-party
library. Instead, that's my agent_tools.py
file. And in there I just have some helper
functions. Functions are just code snippets
that can be executed on demand. A summarize
text function,
some other helper functions, and a build PDF
function and a create PDF function, which
uses build PDF under the hood, which will
just do what their name implies. Create PDF
uses this more complex logic here to create
a PDF file. And summarize text uses an AI
model,
in my case here again, an OpenAI model. And
we could use a cheaper one too, by the way,
for generating a summary based on some
summary instructions, which are set up here,
which basically tell the model how to create
summaries.
And then that summary is returned. And
that's important. A tool, when you write
agents in code, is typically just a
function.
And a function is a construct in programming
languages, which defines a code snippet that
will be executed on demand. That may receive
input and that may
return output. And that's pretty much the
definition of a tool. A tool is some logic
that should be executed when the tool is
needed, that may also use input depending on
the tool, and that may also produce some
output, again, depending on the tool.
And that's why functions are perfect tools
for agents when building agents in code.
So the summarize text tool has all the logic
needed for creating a summary, and it does
not care how it's invoked or if it's being
used in a workflow or by an agent, but we
know that we will use it as a tool for an
agent.
So in there I have some deterministic logic
in the end where I use an AI model for
creating a summary, handling errors, and
returning the summary. And again, we don't
care about the agent in here at all.
And the same is true for all the other code
in agent_tools.
In agent.py, on the other hand, that
changes. There we're importing these tools
and we'll use them and connect them to the
agent further down.
